messages:
Jenna Ortiz: looping you all in — AcmeCorp SLA alert: p99 ~18s, p95 ~4.5s starting ~2024-11-03T17:03Z. Customer timed out and opened a ticket. Stacktrace not exposed but they gave timestamps.

Alice Park: thanks. Which route/model/tenant? any error codes from client?

Jenna Ortiz: route `/v1/generate`, model `redwood-4c`, tenant `acme`. Client saw HTTP 504s and long tails. Our metrics show queue length spiked to ~120 and admission dropped ~30% at 17:03. p99 correlates with queue >80.

Samir Patel: I'm oncall. Pulling dashboards — https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ingress/tenant-metrics (link to panel). Node `node-gpu-07` GPU util 98%, worker-side queue timers high.

Marco Liu: checking logs. I see sustained inflight >32 for that tenant (concurrency cap is 32). We also have a burst of many short requests (small prompt sizes). Auth DB also shows an increased median from 20ms -> 200ms at the same window (possible token refresh storm).

Alice Park: any recent changes? batching/quantization/route config?

Samir Patel: No code deploys at 17:00. Ops note: A config change bumping default batch window for r4c planned yesterday might be live — could explain worker saturation.

Jenna Ortiz: customer provided repro steps (they spammed 1000 tiny requests across 50 clients). Repro from their side:
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-4c","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
done
wait
```
They said p99 appears within seconds.

infra-bot: runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/queueing-backpressure — follow tenant isolation + circuit actions.

Marco Liu: propose immediate mitigations: 
1) Temporarily raise tenant concurrency cap for `acme` from 32 -> 64 to drain queue.
2) Reroute `acme` traffic to `burst-reserve` pool (has spare capacity).
3) Enable soft-fail fast-path for low-priority short requests (drop after queue threshold).
4) Reboot `node-gpu-07` if KV-cache thrash persists.

Commands: 
`redwoodctl tenancy set-concurrency --tenant acme --concurrency 64`
`redwoodctl route update --tenant acme --pool burst-reserve`
`kubectl rollout restart deployment/worker-node-gpu-07 -n prod`

Alice Park: applying step 1 now (running `redwoodctl set-concurrency`).

Alice Park: done — concurrency=64. Queue length: 120 -> 34 in ~45s. p99 dropped from ~18s -> ~2.1s (prelim). :thumbsup:

Jenna Ortiz: notified customer with interim update, they're testing and see improvement. Will keep them in the loop.

Samir Patel: good. Longer-term actions: add auto-burst policy for heavy tenants, strengthen auth DB caching & token refresh debouncing, add alert playbook for per-tenant queue>50 and p99>5s. Opened infra ticket: INFRA-9877.

Marco Liu: also revert the batch-window bump for r4c and roll forward a more conservative setting — file: config/batching/2024-11-02-r4c.yaml.

Alice Park: noted. Any need to escalate to Eng Runtime?

Samir Patel: we'll loop eng-runtime if queue returns or GPU util stays >90% after plan. For now mark as resolved for immediate customer impact; follow-up required.

Jenna Ortiz: closing loop on ticket ACME-1234 (customer confirmed improved perf). Follow-up tasks assigned to INFRA-9877 and ENGRT-453.

Alice Park: thanks team. Filing short postmortem w/links to graphs & commands.

Marco Liu: adding a short reproduction note to the runbook: "small-prompt high-concurrency -> inflight tenant saturation -> long wait in admission queue" and a recommended mitigation checklist.

Samir Patel: ok motioned. I'll keep the alert thresholds on watch for 24h. :eyes:
